chunk_findings.detail: `_cli_vocabulary` inspects `action.choices` which can contain string choices rather than parser objects, causing `stack.extend(action.choices.values())` to raise an `AttributeError` (since strings lack a `_actions` attribute, which leads to `AttributeError` when `stack.pop()` subsequently processes it and accesses `p._actions`). Given a subparsers configuration where choices include string identifiers or non-parser objects, `main()` crashes on invocation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:438

chunk_findings.detail: `recent` only slices when `n > 0`. Given `n=0` (or any negative count) and a log of 500 records, the `if n > 0` guard is skipped and the function returns every parsed record, not the last 0. A repro bundle that asks for no command events therefore embeds the whole ring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cmdlog.py:91

chunk_findings.detail: `record` documents that it never raises, but `int(code)` (and the argv/tail redaction) run before the `OSError` handler. Given `code=None`, `int(None)` raises `TypeError` and aborts the command being logged instead of dropping the record.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cmdlog.py:61

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI entry point and the post_tool hook are both writers, but `_trim` is a non-atomic read-then-`write_text`. Interleaving: process A `open("a")` and writes a line; process B `read_text`s, then `write_text` truncates and rewrites; A's append lands at the old offset or is dropped. The jsonl gains a torn line or loses the newest record, and the next `recent` skips the corrupt line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cmdlog.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: `_cli_vocabulary` puts every `option_strings` entry into `flags`, including store_true / store_const switches such as `--json` and `-h`. This change's own contract (`test_a_value_typed_after_a_kept_flag_keeps_only_its_shape` and the `--note` round-trip) is that a kept flag always consumes the next argv token as `<value>`. Given `ddflow --json list task`, `record` therefore stores something like `["ddflow", "--json", "<value>", "<arg>"]` and drops the verb `list`, so the repro bundle's "last N commands" is not the command that ran.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_cli_vocabulary

chunk_findings.detail: `_remember_command` is only called on the path that returns `code` after a successful `parse_args`. `parser.parse_args` still raises `SystemExit` for unknown verbs and bad flags (exit 2) and that handler is unchanged, so those invocations are never appended. Given argv `["not-a-command"]`, the process exits 2 and `.ddflow/local/cmdlog.jsonl` has no row, which is exactly the failure a repro bundle is supposed to list.

chunk_findings.detail: Concurrent writers lose or corrupt records. `record` appends then `_trim` does an unlocked read-modify-write (`read_text` / `write_text` of the last `CAP_ENTRIES` lines). Two CLI or hook processes can interleave: process A appends, reads a snapshot past the cap, process B appends its JSON line, then A rewrites the file from its snapshot and B's record is gone. The same rewrite can also tear a line B is appending, so `recent` later skips a truncated JSON line and the repro bundle omits a command that did run.
